L437: For lanmodulin, a significant role of metal-binding cooperativity has been demonstrated to account for the protein's high affinity for lanthanides [cite48†27 , cite53†32 ], as well as the role of interprotein interactions in the selectivity for certain lanthanides in the Hans-LanM lanmodulin [cite49†28 ]. Positive cooperativity in lanthanide binding also appears to explain the increased affinity and properties of double-lanthanide-binding tags [cite99†64 ].
L438: In this context, a key perspective of this work is to analyze the binding properties of lanthanides on calmodulin Site 2 before investigating the cooperative and selective properties of an N-terminal domain of calmodulin bearing two LBT-type sites.
L439: ## 4 Experimental Section
L440: 
L441: ### 4.1 Materials
L442: 
L443: All solutions were prepared with analytical grade salts dissolved in 18 MΩ water.
L444: ### 4.2 Engineering and Purification of the Proteins
L445: The sequence of the CaM1 DNA obtained by Pardoux et al. [cite54†33 ] was used as a template for CaMLBT engineering. CaM1 DNA sequence corresponds to the sequence of Arabidopsis thaliana CaM N-terminal domain, modified to include a tyrosine at position 7 and two alanines at positions 10 and 11 of Site 1 binding loop as well as two alanines at positions 1 and 3 of Site 2, to impair metal binding at Site 2 [cite54†33 ].
L446: The sequence coding for the CaMLBT peptide was obtained by two rounds of site-directed mutagenesis.
L447: The site-directed mutations were performed using the QuickChange site-directed mutagenesis kit (Stratagene) following the supplier's instructions and specific primer pairs (for PCR 1, reverse 5′-GCT TTC AGC TTA TTC GAC ACC AAC AAC GAT GGT TAC ATT ACC GCC-3′ and forward 5′-GGC GGT AAT GTA ACC ATC GTT GTT GGT GTC GAA TAA GCT GAA AGC-3′; for PCR 2, reverse 5′-GCT TTC AGC TTA TTC GAC ACC AAC AAC GAT GGT TAC ATT ACC GCC-3′ and forward 5′-GGC GGT AAT GTA ACC ATC GTT GTT GGT GTC GAA TAA GCT GAA AGC-3′).
L448: The TEV protease recognition site was inserted upstream of the coding sequence of CaMLBT and downstream a His-tag in the pQE30 plasmid. After purification, the amino acid sequence of the CaMLBT was the following: SMADQLTDDQISEFKEAFSLFDTNNDGYIEGDELGTVMRSLGQNPTEAELQDMINEVAAAGNGTIDFPEFLNLMARK, with the sequences of Site 1 and Site 2 given in bold character.
L449: Expression and purification of the recombinant CaMLBT peptide were performed almost as previously described [cite54†33 ]. Protein purification involved two steps on HiTrap chelating columns, before and after removal of the His-tag by incubation of the protein overnight at 4°C with TEV protease. A last step of purification was performed on a Sephadex 75 column. The CaMLBT peptide samples were concentrated by using a Microcon filtration system (Amicon Millipore) with a cut-off point of 3 kDa.
L450: Peptide concentrations were measured according to the BC Assay (Uptima) with bovine serum albumin as the standard.
L451: To remove any trace of metal from the samples, the CaMLBT protein was treated with EDTA for 30 min at 4°C (with a peptide/EDTA ratio of 10) followed by subsequent dilution/concentration steps in 20 mM MES pH 6, 100 mM NaCl using using Amicon microcon filtration systems. The buffers were treated with Chelex-100 (1% for 6 h) to remove any traces of calcium or other divalent cations. For CE-ICP-MS experiments, the CaMLBT peptide was dialyzed against MES 57 mM, 80 mM NaCl at pH 6.

L343: #### 2.2.2 Measurement of Ln-CaMLBT Dissociation Constants Using CE-ICP-MS
L344: The dissociation constants of complexes formed between CaMLBT and Pr, Nd, Sm, Eu, and Yb were also measured using CE-ICP-MS in 20 mM MES pH 6 and NTA at 100 µM or 1 mM, as described in the Experimental Section. In these experiments, there is a competition between NTA and the protein to bind Ln(III). This technique, which uses very small concentrations of metals, was previously set-up to measure interactions of transferrin or fetuin with Pu [cite70†39 , cite71†40 ]. The results are given in Table cite62†1 .`
L345: For Yb, the system consistently exhibited two distinct peaks corresponding to Yb-(NTA)_{2}^{3–} and Yb-CaMLBT, as shown in Figure cite72†3A . Both species are negatively charged. Since the two species are always present, their mobilities should remain constant regardless of the protein concentration. This was confirmed using a dataset based on 15 experiments.
L471: The Origin 8.0Pro software (OriginLab Corporation, Northampton MA, USA) was used for the CE-ICPMS data treatment. Two types of processing were done, depending on the Ln: treatment by peak areas when the resolution was sufficient to distinguish two peaks (Yb–CaMLBT interaction), and treatment by determining the mobility of the barycenter of the average peak for CaMLBT interaction with the other Ln. All mobilities are expressed in units of electrophoretic mobility, i.e., ×10^{8} m^{2}·V^{−1}·s^{−1}.
L472: ### 4.6 ATR-FTIR Spectroscopy
L473: The FTIR spectra were recorded on a Bruker IFS66 spectrometer equipped with a DTGS-KBr detector and an attenuated total reflection (ATR) device fitted with a nine-bounce diamond microprism (4.3 mm surface diameter, ZnSe optics, SensIR Technologies, CT). Each spectrum corresponded to 50 co-added scans recorded at a resolution of 4 cm^{−1}. All frequencies are reported with an accuracy of ≈1 cm^{−1}.
L474: The FTIR spectra were recorded with 2–3 µL of the different CaMLBT and Ln-CaMLBT samples at circa 1 mM in MES 20 mM pH 6, deposited and dried on the ATR crystal, to reach an absorption ≤1 at 1650 cm^{−1} (which corresponds to the main protein absorption Amide I region).
L475: Sample preparation was optimized to avoid IR bands dues to differences in relative concentrations of protein and MES buffer in the FTIR difference spectra and effects due to slight changes in pH in the different samples. Therefore, all samples were prepared from the same CaMLBT solution, treated by EDTA and resuspended in a chelex-treated MES buffer at 20 mM pH 6.
L476: All metals added were diluted in water to from equally concentrated solutions in 1% HNO_{3} solution, and the same volume of HNO_{3} diluted in water was added for Apo CaMLBT. The difference spectra were calculated using the OPUS software.
